# Rotated automatic-line baseline isolation

`origins.docx` is an original six-page control generated by
`tools/cell_text_direction_origins_fixture.py` from the existing hand-authored
height control. Each page pairs `btLr` and `tbRl` cells with Arial 10pt,
single automatic line spacing, an exact 60pt row and six forced lines.
Four pages repeat `a`, `Al`, `ph` or `ta`; two reorder mixed strings.
No production document or proprietary font outline is embedded.

`origins-native.pdf` was exported by the reference application.
`origins-reference.json` retains text matrices,
vector bounds and both input/output hashes. All six pages have exactly
the same native baseline X coordinates in each direction:

| Direction | Baselines (pt) |
| --- | --- |
| btLr | 87.504, 99.264, 111.14, 122.9, 134.78, 146.54 |
| tbRl | 266.57, 254.69, 243.05, 231.05, 219.41, 207.41 |

The engine's third and fifth `tbRl` baselines differ by approximately
0.209pt and 0.192pt on **every** page. This reproduces the height control's
discrepancy independently of glyph selection, glyph order and automatic
wrapping. It does not establish the correct general positioning formula,
nor does it justify a glyph-specific offset or a looser tolerance.

The browser layout test verifies native invariance, source text, wrapping,
page count and Y positions before checking the exact known X failures.
The final assertion remains an expected failure: this is diagnostic evidence,
not a successful fidelity comparison. No renderer behavior changed.

ECMA-376 Part 1 section 17.4.72 defines table-cell text direction. These
controls investigate the native reference positioning; they do not establish a contradiction
between the reference application and a normative baseline formula in that section.

Regenerate from the repository root (use the available Python interpreter):

```powershell
python tools/cell_text_direction_origins_fixture.py
powershell -NoProfile -File tools/export-reference.ps1 -SourceFullPath "$PWD/tests/fixtures/cell-text-direction/origins.docx" -OutputPdf "$PWD/tests/fixtures/cell-text-direction/origins-native.pdf"
python tools/record_cell_text_direction.py origins
```

The next unresolved question is how the reference application rounds cross-axis coordinates for
`tbRl`. The repeated controls rule out character-dependent compensation.
The paired native captures now recorded under `origin-phase` reproduce the
nonmonotonic shifts before PDF serialization, ruling out a PDF-only explanation.
They still do not distinguish layout rounding from a shared drawing/export
calculation, or establish live-screen rasterization. No formula is justified yet.
